Links: [{"title":"Securing your API","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api"},{"title":"Securing your data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data"},{"title":"Database","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview"},{"title":"RAG with Permissions","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/rag-with-permissions"},{"title":"Tables and data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/tables"},{"title":"Auth","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth"},{"title":"API keys","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys"},{"title":"Supabase Docs","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/storage-error-403-forbidden-new-row-violates-row-level-security-policy-on-upload-a94384"},{"title":"Realtime Authorization","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/authorization"},{"title":"Production Checklist","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod"}]

Supabase's docs cover Row Level Security (RLS) in several guides. The core pages are the "Row Level Security" guide under Access and security, the "Securing your API" guide, and the "Tables and data" guide.

- **Core model:** RLS is how Supabase keeps the database safe to query directly from client apps. The main guide is linked from the Database overview (Row Level Security (RLS) is how Supabase makes the database safe to query directly from the client. Read this before exposing any table to your app.)
- **Two layers of access:** Grants decide which roles (anon, authenticated, service_role) can reach an object at all, while RLS policies decide which rows those roles can touch. The docs say to use both for every exposed object (Use both controls for every exposed object.).
- **Getting started with tables:** RLS must be enabled on each table, then a policy added. Until a policy exists, Data API requests return no rows (Until one exists, Data API requests return no rows.). The docs include a worked example with per-user watchlists using `auth.uid()`.
- **Keys and roles:** Publishable keys map to the anon or authenticated role depending on sign-in state, while secret keys bypass RLS through service_role (Policies never apply to a secret key, because service_role has the BYPASSRLS attribute.).
- **Debugging:** A missing grant produces a permission error, while a policy matching no rows returns an empty result, so check grants first (A missing grant returns a permission error, including for service_role, whereas a policy that matches no rows returns an empty result. Check the grant before you debug the policy.).
- **Performance:** The "Row Level Security Performance" page is listed separately in the Database overview. The Securing your API guide also warns that functions called inside policies are evaluated per row and can slow queries.
- **Production:** The Production Checklist says to enable RLS on all tables before going live (Tables that do not have RLS enabled with reasonable policies allow any client to access and modify their data.).

The results also include RLS pages for Realtime authorization (policies on `realtime.messages`) and for RAG/pgvector permissions. The search returned only overview and excerpt text, not full guide pages, so for complete policy syntax and examples, open the "Row Level Security" guide at supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security.
